resources.string: No audio input: All audio samples are zero!
eInk Birding needs to download the BirdNET model (~ 39MB). \n No commercial use allowed \n(CC-BY-NC-SA 4.0 license)
Keep the sound of each detection, so tapping its row plays back what was heard. About 288KB each, in the app\'s own storage rather than in your music.
Not listening. Nothing is being recorded.
List a bird heard over and over as one line for the run, or as every hearing with its own time.
Put the picture of the last bird heard clearly at the top of the listening screen. It stays there until a different bird is heard as clearly.
Throw away the model\'s non-bird answers: people, dogs, engines, sirens, tools and plain noise.
Delete the log — tap again to confirm
Draw the shape of the recording under the photograph when a row is opened: time across, pitch up, loud dark.
Keep recordings for this session only
Throw the recordings away the next time the app starts, rather than letting them build up.

A fork of whoBIRD by woheller69, under the GNU General Public Licence, version 3.

Identification is BirdNET, by Stefan Kahl, Connor Wood, Maximilian Eibl and Holger Klinck, of the Cornell Lab of Ornithology and Chemnitz University of Technology. The models are licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and may not be used commercially.

Photographs come from the Macaulay Library at the Cornell Lab of Ornithology.

Every recording is identified on this phone. Nothing is sent anywhere; the one thing this app fetches is a bird's photograph, and only for a bird whose row you open.
